about: Research sheet for the Rhode Island county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Rhode Island
phones_sentence: Rhode Island has one statewide Veterans Resource Center, run by the Office of Veterans Services in Warwick; every county shows it.

offices.source_title: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services: About Us
offices.note: The Office of Veterans Services offers benefits counseling and help applying for VA and state programs at no charge.
offices.selection: Rhode Island has no county veterans offices. The Office of Veterans Services’ About Us page (read in full) places the statewide Veterans Resource Center at 560 Jefferson Boulevard in Warwick but lists no phone; the phone, 401-921-2119, comes from the office’s 2021 statement (https://vets.ri.gov/press-releases/rivets-statement-services-and-supports-vets-military-families) and the suite number from the Division of Motor Vehicles’ veteran contacts (https://dmv.ri.gov/node/881), both search excerpts. Every county shows this one office.

aging.source_title: Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging: Aging and Disability Resource Center (The Point)
aging.source_scope: ADRC line (401) 462-4444, answered 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in Spanish and with interpreters for 100+ languages; read in full. The page lists no office locations. Other sources (search excerpts): the Point is for people 55 and older, adults living with a disability and caregivers (https://oha.ri.gov/get-help); TTY (401) 462-4445 or 2-1-1, and six Point offices (https://dhs.ri.gov/programs-and-services/long-term-services-and-supports/resources); the main Point office is at 50 Valley St., Providence, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. (https://www.unitedwayri.org/get-help/point/). Regional Point offices serve groups of towns, not counties, so every county shows the statewide line.
aging.description: The Point, Rhode Island’s Aging and Disability Resource Center, run by the Office of Healthy Aging with United Way: free, confidential help for people 55 and older, adults with disabilities and caregivers to find services and apply for public and private programs, from help at home and meals to caregiver support and long-term care options.
aging.next_step_extra: The line answers 24 hours a day (TTY 401-462-4445, or dial 2-1-1). You can also visit the Point at 50 Valley St., Providence, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.; ask which regional Point office is nearest you.

programs.name: Rhode Island veterans: Office of Veterans Services (RIVETS) Veterans Resource Center
programs.organization: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services (RIVETS)
programs.description: The statewide Veterans Resource Center in Warwick offers benefits counseling, help with discharge papers and help applying for VA and state programs, plus case management for housing, employment, transportation, health and food needs. Veterans, service members, Guard, Reserve and their families can use it.
programs.next_step: Call 401-921-2119, or complete the RIVets Intake Form on vets.ri.gov to have a representative contact you.
constraints: RIVETS is a state office, not the VA Regional Office or a VA medical center.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (Rhode Island SHIP)
programs.organization: Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
programs.description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Rhode Island’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Office of Healthy Aging and partner agencies across the state, including senior centers in Johnston, Pawtucket, South Kingstown (Wakefield) and Westerly and community agencies in Woonsocket, East Providence, Central Falls and Newport.
programs.next_step: Call the SHIP line at 1-888-884-8721, or call the Point at 401-462-4444. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: Rhode Island Long-Term Care Ombudsman and elder abuse reporting
programs.organization: Office of the Rhode Island State Long Term Care Ombudsman; Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging, Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other care facilities, including reports of suspected abuse in a facility. The Office of Healthy Aging’s Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect, financial exploitation or self-neglect of people 60 and older living in the community.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 401-785-3340 or toll-free 888-351-0808. To report abuse of an older person at home, call Adult Protective Services at 401-462-0555, any time; reports can be anonymous. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free and low-cost legal help for older Rhode Islanders
programs.organization: Rhode Island Legal Services; Rhode Island Bar Association
programs.description: The Office of Healthy Aging lists two legal partners for people 60 and older: Rhode Island Legal Services gives free legal help to lower-income adults 60+ with public-assistance programs, and the Rhode Island Bar Association offers legal help to adults 60+ with fees on a sliding scale.
programs.next_step: Call Rhode Island Legal Services at 401-274-2652 or 800-662-5034. For other legal questions, ask the Point (401-462-4444) for the Bar Association’s senior program.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income and case type.

programs.name: VA health care in Rhode Island
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Providence Healthcare System
programs.description: Rhode Island veterans are served by the VA Providence Healthcare System: the Providence VA Medical Center (830 Chalkstone Avenue, Providence; 401-273-7100) and its community clinics. The Warwick Vet Center (2038 Warwick Ave.; 401-739-0167) offers readjustment counseling.
programs.next_step: Call 401-273-7100 or the local VA call center, 401-457-3336, for appointments. Not enrolled yet? Ask RIVETS for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All five counties show the statewide Veterans Resource Center in Warwick, the Point (the statewide Aging and Disability Resource Center) and the statewide long-term care ombudsman. Kent and Providence counties also show a Center for Independent Living.
coverage_note: Veterans contacts come from the Office of Veterans Services. Aging help comes from the Office of Healthy Aging. Centers for Independent Living come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
